es: Diagnosticar y corregir errores de interacción profesional en cuatro áreas: registro, turnos, seguimiento y tacto.

teaching.en: In a first email to a manager, use a formal register.
teaching.es: En un primer correo a un jefe, usa un registro formal.
teaching.explanationEs: Register = registro: la forma de pedir (Could you…? / I would be grateful if…) debe encajar con quien lee.
segments: In a first email to a
manager, use a formal register.
teaching.audioText: In a first email to a manager, use a formal register.

teaching.en: 'You are wrong' is blunt, but 'I see it slightly differently' is tactful.
teaching.es: «Estás equivocado» es brusco, pero «Yo lo veo de forma algo distinta» es diplomático.
teaching.explanationEs: Blunt = brusco, sin suavizar; tactful = con tacto. El contenido puede ser el mismo.
segments: 'You are wrong' is blunt, but 'I
see it slightly differently' is tactful.
teaching.audioText: 'You are wrong' is blunt, but 'I see it slightly differently' is tactful.

teaching.en: Sorry to interrupt, but may I add one point before we move on?
teaching.es: Perdona que interrumpa, pero ¿puedo añadir un punto antes de pasar al siguiente?
teaching.explanationEs: Sorry to + verbo pide paso con cortesía; «perdona por interrumpir» no se traduce con for + verbo.
segments: Sorry to interrupt, but may I add
one point before we move on?
teaching.audioText: Sorry to interrupt, but may I add one point before we move on?

teaching.en: Let me finish this point, and then it is your turn.
teaching.es: Déjame terminar este punto y luego es tu turno.
teaching.explanationEs: Turn = turno de palabra: cada persona termina su idea antes de que empiece otra.
segments: Let me finish this point, and
then it is your turn.
teaching.audioText: Let me finish this point, and then it is your turn.

teaching.en: A follow-up question, such as 'What made you choose that city?', shows genuine interest.
teaching.es: Una pregunta de seguimiento, como «¿Qué te hizo elegir esa ciudad?», muestra un interés sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: Follow-up retoma lo que el otro acaba de decir; una pregunta sin relación corta la conversación.
segments: A follow-up question, such as 'What made
you choose that city?', shows genuine interest.
teaching.audioText: A follow-up question, such as 'What made you choose that city?', shows genuine interest.

teaching.en: Before you correct a message, diagnose the problem: register, turns, follow-up or tact?
teaching.es: Antes de corregir un mensaje, diagnostica el problema: ¿registro, turnos, seguimiento o tacto?
teaching.explanationEs: Primero se nombra el área que falla y después se corrige con la fórmula adecuada.
segments: Before you correct a message, diagnose the
problem: register, turns, follow-up or tact?
teaching.audioText: Before you correct a message, diagnose the problem: register, turns, follow-up or tact?

prompt.es: ¿Qué área falla en la respuesta de Tom al señor Silva?

choices.text: Turns: he speaks before the manager finishes.
Register: it is too blunt for a manager.
Tact: he criticises the manager's survey.

feedback.es: Tom le dice «Give me the password» a su jefe sin ninguna fórmula de petición: es un fallo de registro. No hay interrupción ni crítica en el intercambio.

hint.es: Fíjate en cómo pide algo Tom a alguien con más autoridad.

origin.text: Mr Silva: Did you finish the survey? Tom: No. Give me the password.

prompt.es: Completa: «Perdona que interrumpa, ¿puedo hacer una pregunta?»

feedback.es: Para pedir paso se dice sorry to interrupt: sorry + to + verbo, no for.

hint.es: Después de sorry, la acción inmediata lleva to + verbo.

origin.text: Sorry ___ interrupt, but may I ask a question?

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta de Leo es una pregunta de seguimiento sincera?

choices.text: I work in a bank.
Kitchens are boring.
What does a typical day look like there?

feedback.es: Solo «What does a typical day look like there?» retoma lo que dijo Ana y pide más información; las otras dos cortan el tema o lo desprecian.

hint.es: Busca la respuesta que retoma lo que dijo Ana y pide más información.

origin.text: Ana: I work in a hospital kitchen.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Podrías enviarme el informe cuando tengas un momento?»

answer.text: Could you send me the report when you have a moment

feedback.es: La petición cortés empieza con Could you y deja la condición («when you have a moment») al final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo responde Sara al plan de Tom.

choices.text: She disagrees politely and suggests a test.
She agrees and ends the talk.
She interrupts and changes the topic.

feedback.es: Sara no dice «no»: suaviza con «I am not sure it will work» y propone probarlo, así que discrepa con tacto y ofrece un paso práctico.

origin.audio: Tom says: That plan will never work. Sara says: Well, I am not sure it will work. Could we test it first?

prompt.es: Relaciona cada área de la conversación con su pregunta de diagnóstico.

pairs.es: ¿Cada persona termina antes de que hable otra?
¿Se retoma lo que dijo el otro?

feedback.es: Cada área se diagnostica con una pregunta distinta: forma, reparto de la palabra, retomar lo dicho y suavizar.

pairs.es: ¿Cada persona termina antes de que hable otra?
¿Se retoma lo que dijo el otro?

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección arregla el fallo de tacto de Leo?

choices.text: No, June is bad. Change it.
I am not sure June works, because it may be a difficult month.
That is wrong, so choose May.

feedback.es: La versión con «I am not sure…» mantiene la duda sobre junio sin decirle a Sara que está equivocada. Las otras dos siguen siendo bruscas.

origin.text: Sara: I think we should move the launch to June. Leo: No, that is wrong. June is a bad month.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué error comete Tom.

choices.text: His register is too formal for the meeting.
He asks no follow-up question.
He talks over Mia without asking permission.

feedback.es: Tom manda parar a Mia en mitad de su explicación sin pedir turno: es un error de turnos, no de registro ni de seguimiento.

origin.audio: Mia was explaining the budget when Tom said: Stop, that is wrong, listen to me. Mia stopped and looked surprised.

prompt.es: Completa las tres correcciones: petición, turno y seguimiento.

feedback.es: Petición cortés con Could you, turno de palabra con your turn y seguimiento con «What made you…?».

sentences: To a manager: ___ you send me the file, please?
Let me finish this point, and then it is your ___.
That sounds exciting! What ___ you choose that city?

prompt.es: Ordena la corrección: «Me gustaría que me enviaras el archivo.»

answer.text: I would like you to send me the file

feedback.es: Would like + persona + to + verbo corrige el calco «want that you send» y suena más cortés.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta mantiene el registro formal con una clienta?

choices.text: Certainly. I will confirm it by noon.
Fine. Wait there, I am busy.
No idea. Ask someone else.

feedback.es: La clienta escribe con formalidad y «Certainly. I will confirm it by noon» responde en el mismo registro. Las otras dos son coloquiales o bruscas.

origin.text: A client writes: Please confirm the date of the meeting.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le falta a la respuesta de Leo.

choices.text: A more formal register.
A follow-up question about Ana's move.
A polite way to interrupt.

feedback.es: Leo cambia de tema sin retomar la mudanza de Ana: le falta una pregunta de seguimiento. El registro y los turnos no son el problema.

origin.audio: Ana said she moved to Lima last year. Leo replied: Nice. Anyway, what time is lunch?

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo veo de forma algo distinta.»

feedback.es: La fórmula «I see it slightly differently» discrepa con tacto: slightly suaviza y differently evita decir «you are wrong».

origin.text: I see it slightly ___.

es: Repasar con precisión cuatro recursos formales: condicionales sin if, pasivas de reporte, nominalizaciones y lenguaje de proyección.

teaching.en: Should you require further details, please contact the office.
teaching.es: Si necesita más detalles, póngase en contacto con la oficina.
teaching.explanationEs: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a «if you should»: posibilidad futura, registro formal.
segments: Should you require further details,
please contact the office.
teaching.audioText: Should you require further details, please contact the office.

teaching.en: Had we known about the delay, we would have called you.
teaching.es: Si hubiéramos sabido del retraso, te habríamos llamado.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + sujeto + participio sustituye a «if we had known»: pasado irreal y formal.
segments: Had we known about the delay,
we would have called you.
teaching.audioText: Had we known about the delay, we would have called you.

teaching.en: Were the council to approve the budget, work would start in May.
teaching.es: Si el ayuntamiento aprobara el presupuesto, las obras empezarían en mayo.
teaching.explanationEs: Were + sujeto + to + verbo plantea una hipótesis remota, sin if.
segments: Were the council to approve the
budget, work would start in May.
teaching.audioText: Were the council to approve the budget, work would start in May.

teaching.en: The fire is reported to have started in the kitchen.
teaching.es: Se informa de que el incendio empezó en la cocina.
teaching.explanationEs: Is reported to have + participio: el hecho es anterior y la fuente queda general.
segments: The fire is reported to
have started in the kitchen.
teaching.audioText: The fire is reported to have started in the kitchen.

teaching.en: The increase in fares led to a fall in passengers.
teaching.es: El aumento de las tarifas provocó una caída de pasajeros.
teaching.explanationEs: Nominalización: increase y fall son nombres y se construyen con in, no con of.
segments: The increase in fares led
to a fall in passengers.
teaching.audioText: The increase in fares led to a fall in passengers.

teaching.en: Sales are projected to double by 2030, and the company is set to open ten stores.
teaching.es: Se prevé que las ventas se dupliquen para 2030 y la empresa se dispone a abrir diez tiendas.
teaching.explanationEs: Projected to / set to + verbo: proyección apoyada en datos o planes.
segments: Sales are projected to double by 2030, and
the company is set to open ten stores.
teaching.audioText: Sales are projected to double by 2030, and the company is set to open ten stores.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si necesita ayuda, póngase en contacto con Sara.»

feedback.es: Para hablar de una posibilidad futura en registro formal se empieza con Should y se omite if.

hint.es: Empieza la frase formal sin if: auxiliar + sujeto + verbo base.

origin.text: ___ you require help, please contact Sara.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa que el puente cerró en junio, según informes?

choices.text: The bridge is reported to close in June.
The bridge reported to have closed in June.
The bridge is reported to have closed in June.

feedback.es: El cierre es anterior al momento en que se informa, así que se necesita to have + participio: is reported to have closed.

hint.es: El cierre ya ocurrió: necesitas to have + participio.

origin.text: News item: the bridge closed in June, according to several reports.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo se dice «El aumento de los precios provocó una caída de las ventas»?

choices.text: The increase in prices led to a fall in sales.
The increase of prices led to a fall of sales.
The increase in prices led to a fall on sales.

feedback.es: Con increase y fall se usa la preposición in para decir qué cambia: an increase in prices, a fall in sales.

hint.es: Después de increase y fall, la preposición correcta es in.

prompt.es: Ordena: «De haber sabido del examen, habría estudiado más.»

answer.text: Had I known about the exam I would have studied more

feedback.es: Had + sujeto + participio abre la frase formal, y la consecuencia lleva would have + participio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué situación describe el hablante.

choices.text: A fact: the school has closed the library.
A remote possibility: the school might close the library.
A past event: the library closed last year.

feedback.es: Were … to plantea una hipótesis remota: el colegio podría cerrar la biblioteca, pero aún no lo ha hecho.

origin.audio: Were the school to close the library, students would have nowhere quiet to study.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada estructura formal con su significado.

pairs.es: Se informa de que se fue (hecho pasado)

feedback.es: Cada estructura marca un grado distinto de realidad: posibilidad, pasado irreal, previsión y hecho pasado atribuido.

pairs.es: Se informa de que se fue (hecho pasado)

prompt.es: Completa las tres frases formales: condicional, proyección y nominalización.

feedback.es: Should abre el condicional sin if; projected/expected/set to introducen la previsión; y an increase in lleva la preposición in.

sentences: ___ the delay continue, we will cancel the trip.
Prices are ___ to rise by five per cent next year.
An increase ___ fares caused a delay.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sabemos con certeza.

choices.text: That the director confirms the paintings are lost.
That the museum moved the paintings on purpose.
Only that someone reports the loss; it is not confirmed.

feedback.es: «Is reported to have lost» atribuye la noticia a otras fuentes y el director no la ha confirmado: lo único seguro es que se informa de la pérdida.

origin.audio: The museum is reported to have lost two paintings during the move, but the director has not confirmed it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reescritura formal corrige el error de Mia?

choices.text: Had we known the price, we would have chosen another hotel.
Were we to know the price, we would have chosen another hotel.
Having we known the price, we would have chosen another hotel.

feedback.es: El condicional de pasado irreal formal es Had we known…; «if we would have known» no es correcto en inglés estándar y Were cambia el significado y Having we known no existe en inglés.

origin.text: Mia wrote: If we would have known the price, we would have chosen another hotel.

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés formal, sin if: «Si necesita un recibo, avise a la oficina.»

answer.text: Should you need a receipt, please tell the office.
accepted: Should you need a receipt, please tell the office.
Should you require a receipt, please tell the office.
Should you need a receipt, please inform the office.
Should you require a receipt, please inform the office.
Should you need a receipt, please let the office know.

feedback.es: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a if en un aviso formal: Should you need…, seguido de una petición cortés.

origin.text: Si necesita un recibo, avise a la oficina.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión nominalizada condensa mejor la idea?

choices.text: The ten per cent rise of fares led to a fall of travellers.
The ten per cent rise in fares led to a fall in travellers.
Fares rose ten per cent, so travellers fell.

feedback.es: «The ten per cent rise in fares led to a fall in travellers» convierte los dos verbos en nombres con in. La versión con of calca el español.

origin.text: Report: Fares rose by ten per cent, so fewer people travelled.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ocurrió en realidad.

choices.text: The team trained a lot and won.
The team has not played the final yet.
The team did not train enough and lost.

feedback.es: Had the team trained more, they would have won es pasado irreal: el equipo no entrenó lo bastante y perdió la final.

origin.audio: Had the team trained more, they would have won the final.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si el ayuntamiento aprobara el plan, las obras empezarían pronto.»

feedback.es: Were + sujeto + to + verbo plantea una hipótesis remota: Were the council to approve…

origin.text: Were the council ___ approve the plan, work would start soon.

es: Analizar el tono, la postura y las implicaciones de un fragmento de pódcast o de una canción, citando la pista que lo demuestra.

teaching.en: The host sounds sceptical: she says the plan will 'supposedly' save money.
teaching.es: La presentadora suena escéptica: dice que el plan «supuestamente» ahorrará dinero.
teaching.explanationEs: Supposedly pone distancia: el hablante no se compromete con que sea verdad.
segments: The host sounds sceptical: she says
the plan will 'supposedly' save money.
teaching.audioText: The host sounds sceptical: she says the plan will 'supposedly' save money.

teaching.en: In the second verse the singer's tone is wistful: she remembers a street that no longer exists.
teaching.es: En la segunda estrofa el tono de la cantante es nostálgico: recuerda una calle que ya no existe.
teaching.explanationEs: Tone = tono: la emoción del hablante, no solo lo que dice. Wistful es añoranza suave.
segments: In the second verse the singer's tone is wistful:
she remembers a street that no longer exists.
teaching.audioText: In the second verse the singer's tone is wistful: she remembers a street that no longer exists.

teaching.en: 'Lovely weather for a picnic,' he said in the pouring rain, in an ironic voice.
teaching.es: «Qué tiempo tan agradable para un picnic», dijo bajo la lluvia torrencial, con voz irónica.
teaching.explanationEs: Ironic = irónico: lo dicho es lo contrario de lo que se piensa y el contexto lo revela.
segments: 'Lovely weather for a picnic,' he said in
the pouring rain, in an ironic voice.
teaching.audioText: 'Lovely weather for a picnic,' he said in the pouring rain, in an ironic voice.

teaching.en: Saying the film is 'hardly a masterpiece' may imply that it is weak.
teaching.es: Decir que la película «no es precisamente una obra maestra» puede dar a entender que es floja.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply = dar a entender: la idea no se dice, se deduce. Hardly resta valor a la palabra siguiente.
segments: Saying the film is 'hardly a masterpiece'
may imply that it is weak.
teaching.audioText: Saying the film is 'hardly a masterpiece' may imply that it is weak.

teaching.en: A dismissive guest answers 'Whatever' and changes the subject, so his stance is clear.
teaching.es: Un invitado despectivo responde «Lo que sea» y cambia de tema, así que su postura es clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Dismissive = rechaza sin argumentar. Stance = postura: la actitud del hablante ante el tema.
segments: A dismissive guest answers 'Whatever' and changes
the subject, so his stance is clear.
teaching.audioText: A dismissive guest answers 'Whatever' and changes the subject, so his stance is clear.

teaching.en: To find the stance, ask who speaks, what they stress and what they leave out.
teaching.es: Para hallar la postura, pregunta quién habla, qué destaca y qué deja fuera.
teaching.explanationEs: Tres preguntas de análisis: la voz, el énfasis y lo que se omite.
segments: To find the stance, ask who speaks, what
they stress and what they leave out.
teaching.audioText: To find the stance, ask who speaks, what they stress and what they leave out.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tono transmite la presentadora con supposedly en esta frase?

choices.text: Sceptical: she keeps her distance from the claim.
Wistful: she remembers a better past.
Ironic: she says the opposite of what she thinks.

feedback.es: Supposedly pone distancia: la presentadora no se compromete con la promesa del ayuntamiento, así que su tono es escéptico. Ni añora el pasado ni dice lo contrario de lo que piensa.

hint.es: Supposedly pone distancia: ¿la presentadora se cree lo que dice el ayuntamiento?

origin.text: Podcast host: The council says the new bus lane will supposedly cut delays by half.

prompt.es: Completa: «En la segunda estrofa, el tono de la cantante es nostálgico.»

feedback.es: Wistful describe una añoranza suave, por eso encaja con una cantante que recuerda un lugar que ya no está.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo para el tono de quien recuerda algo del pasado con suave tristeza.

origin.text: In the second verse, the singer's tone is ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la crítica sin decirlo directamente?

choices.text: That the film is a masterpiece.
That the film is weak.
That the film is very long.

feedback.es: «Hardly a masterpiece» resta valor a masterpiece: la crítica sugiere que la película es floja, aunque no use esa palabra.

hint.es: Hardly resta valor a la palabra que lo sigue.

origin.text: Reviewer: The new film is hardly a masterpiece.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué tono usa Leo.

choices.text: Wistful: he misses sunny days.
Enthusiastic: he enjoys the rain.
Ironic: the weather is actually bad.

feedback.es: Leo dice que hace buen tiempo estando bajo una lluvia fuerte: el tono es irónico, porque lo dicho es lo contrario de la situación.

origin.audio: Lovely weather for a picnic, said Leo, standing in the pouring rain with a wet sandwich.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada tono con su descripción.

pairs.es: Duda de que lo dicho sea verdad
Dice lo contrario de lo que piensa

feedback.es: Cada adjetivo nombra una actitud distinta: duda, añoranza, rechazo sin argumentos y contradicción entre lo dicho y lo pensado.

pairs.es: Duda de que lo dicho sea verdad
Dice lo contrario de lo que piensa

prompt.es: Ordena: «La presentadora da a entender que el plan es demasiado caro.»

answer.text: The host implies that the plan is too expensive

feedback.es: Imply + that + oración: la presentadora no dice «it is too expensive» sino que lo sugiere con su comentario.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura tiene la presentadora sobre el parque.

choices.text: She doubts that it is a success, and she shows it by joking.
She believes that it is a big success.
She has no opinion and only reports the facts.

feedback.es: La presentadora cita solo cuarenta visitantes en una ciudad enorme y termina con un comentario exagerado: duda, con ironía, de que sea un éxito.

origin.audio: Today's guest says the new park is a big success. Apparently, forty people visited it last Sunday. Forty. In a city of two million. But I am sure it will be great once the trees grow.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tono domina en esta estrofa?

choices.text: Angry, with open complaints.
Wistful, with a gentle acceptance.
Playful, with a joke about the shop.

feedback.es: La cantante recuerda la panadería de su calle con una sonrisa y acepta que todo cambia: hay añoranza (wistful) sin enfado ni burla.

origin.text: The bakery on Maple Street is a phone shop now. I still turn left there, out of habit, and smile. Nothing stays, but I do not mind: I kept the smell of bread.

prompt.es: Completa el análisis: tono, implicación y actitud del invitado.

feedback.es: Un análisis completo nombra el tono (sceptical), la implicación (imply) y la actitud de quien rechaza sin argumentos (dismissive).

sentences: The host says 'supposedly', so her tone is ___.
'Hardly a masterpiece' may ___ that the film is weak.
A ___ guest says 'Whatever' and changes the subject.

prompt.es: ¿Qué deja entender el crítico al hablar solo del vestíbulo y del uniforme?

choices.text: That the room was excellent.
That the lobby was closed.
That the room was poor.

feedback.es: Cuando un crítico elogia detalles menores y calla sobre lo principal, la omisión sugiere una decepción: aquí, que la habitación no estuvo a la altura.

origin.text: Reviewer: The hotel has a lovely lobby, and the staff wore clean uniforms. The room? It had a bed.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué implica la cantante.

choices.text: She is not really fine.
She is very happy.
She is angry with the band.

feedback.es: Repetir «I am fine» mientras la voz se quiebra da a entender lo contrario: no está bien. La pista es el contraste entre la letra y la voz.

origin.audio: The singer repeats I am fine four times in the chorus, but her voice breaks on the last word.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de la presentadora ante la promesa del alcalde?

choices.text: She fully trusts the mayor.
She doubts the mayor's promise.
She is wistful about the old mayor.

feedback.es: «We will see» cierra la cita con distancia: la presentadora no cree la promesa. No confía plenamente ni añora a otro alcalde.

origin.text: Host: The mayor promises, and I quote, 'a new era'. We will see.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su tono es irónico.»

feedback.es: Decir «qué gran idea» ante un puente roto es lo contrario de lo que se piensa: tono irónico.

origin.text: 'What a great idea,' she said, looking at the broken bridge. Her tone is ___.

title.en: Storytelling project: a story with a purpose

es: Escribir una historia de 220 a 270 palabras con gancho, tensión, giro, recursos de énfasis y una reflexión final.

teaching.en: A good hook puts the reader in the middle of a moment: I still remember the night I missed the last train.
teaching.es: Un buen gancho pone al lector en medio de un momento: Todavía recuerdo la noche en que perdí el último tren.
teaching.explanationEs: El gancho abre con un momento concreto, no con una explicación del tema.
segments: A good hook puts the reader in the middle of a
moment: I still remember the night I missed the last train.
teaching.audioText: A good hook puts the reader in the middle of a moment: I still remember the night I missed the last train.

teaching.en: Tension builds when the narrator gives a clue and delays the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.
teaching.es: La tensión crece cuando el narrador da una pista y retrasa la respuesta: la estación estaba vacía y entonces oí pasos.
teaching.explanationEs: Clue + delay: primero la pista (empty, footsteps) y después, más tarde, la explicación.
segments: Tension builds when the narrator gives a clue and delays the
answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.
teaching.audioText: Tension builds when the narrator gives a clue and delays the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.

teaching.en: The twist changes how we read the story: the stranger turned out to be my new teacher.
teaching.es: El giro cambia cómo leemos la historia: el desconocido resultó ser mi nuevo profesor.
teaching.explanationEs: Turn out to be = resultar ser: el giro revela algo que el lector no esperaba.
segments: The twist changes how we read the story: the
stranger turned out to be my new teacher.
teaching.audioText: The twist changes how we read the story: the stranger turned out to be my new teacher.

teaching.en: For emphasis, say 'It was the silence that frightened me' or 'Never had I felt so relieved'.
teaching.es: Para dar énfasis, di «Lo que me asustó fue el silencio» o «Nunca me había sentido tan aliviado».
teaching.explanationEs: Cleft: It was + lo destacado + that. Inversión: Never had I + participio. Úsalas una o dos veces.

answer.text: I still remember the night I missed the last train. I was a student, and I had spent the whole evening at a friend's birthday party in the next town. When I reached the station, the platform was empty and the clock showed midnight. My phone had no battery, and the nearest taxi was far away. I sat on a cold bench and tried to stay calm. It was not the dark that frightened me; it was the silence. Never had I heard a city so quiet. Then, behind me, I heard footsteps. They were slow, and they were coming closer. I held my bag tightly and did not look back. 'Are you waiting for the last train?' a voice asked. I looked up, and my heart stopped. The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

I held my bag tightly and did not look back. 'Are you waiting for the last train?' a voice asked. I looked up, and my heart stopped. The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

The night I missed the last train began like any other. I was at a party in the next town, and I left too late. On the platform, the clock showed midnight and nobody was there. I sat down and waited, because my phone had no battery. What frightened me most was the silence. Then I heard footsteps behind me, slow and close. I did not dare to look. The lights were weak, and the wind moved some old paper along the ground. A voice said, 'Are you waiting for the last train?' I looked up, and there was my new science teacher, Mr Duarte, in a long grey coat. It turned out that he lived nearby, and he offered me a lift home. In the car we hardly spoke, but it was warm, and the radio played softly. I felt almost ashamed. I had been afraid of a man who only wanted to help. Looking back, I learned that I often expect the worst when I am alone. Never again will I stay silent when I need help.

answer.text: Dear Mr Reid, Good morning. I am a newcomer to the city, and I am writing about the flat on Elm Street. I can pay the deposit now, provided that the rent is 650 a month instead of 700. In exchange for the lower rent, I would sign a twelve-month contract. I also think there was a misunderstanding about the floor: I meant the second floor, not the first. Let me clarify this now so that we can avoid any problem later. Thank you very much for your patience, and I look forward to your reply. Kind regards, Carlos
